name: Stationary Cycling
summary: Pedal an indoor stationary bicycle to build cardiovascular endurance and lower-body muscular stamina.

setup: Adjust the saddle height so there is a slight bend in the knee (roughly 25 to 35 degrees) when the pedal is at the lowest point of the stroke.
Adjust the handlebar height and reach to allow a comfortable forward hinge from the hips without rounding your spine excessively.
Step onto the bike, sit firmly on the saddle, and secure your feet into the pedals or toe cages.
steps: Begin pedaling smoothly in a continuous circular motion, pushing down through the ball of the foot and drawing through the bottom of the stroke.
Maintain a steady rhythm, keeping your knees tracking inline with your toes.
Keep a relaxed grip on the handlebars and avoid collapsing your weight onto your wrists.
Adjust the resistance and cadence to achieve the desired training intensity.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and rhythmically, matching your breathing pace to your cadence and effort level.

common_faults.fault: Saddle set too low or too high.
common_faults.correction: Adjust the seat height to ensure a slight bend in the knee at the bottom of the pedal stroke to avoid joint strain.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing in the saddle at high cadence.
common_faults.correction: Increase the magnetic or flywheel resistance slightly to stabilize the pedal stroke.

common_faults.fault: Excessive weight bearing on handlebars with hunched shoulders.
common_faults.correction: Support your upper body through your core and hips while keeping a light, relaxed grip.

precautions: Ensure all seat and handlebar adjustment pins are securely locked into place before starting.
